description: Sanctions screening is embedded in ordinary commercial onboarding, not just banking.
Common Persian names collide with sanctions-list entries, producing repeated manual review the customer must resolve by proving who they are not.
Refusals cite internal policy. Without a stated reason there is nothing to appeal and no evidence of a pattern.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the name that trips the screen
description: Common Persian names collide with sanctions-list entries, so an ordinary purchase, tenancy check or payroll onboarding drops into manual review and the customer must prove they are not a listed person.
energy_note: Proving a negative about a stranger with your name.

description: Rental and insurance underwriting runs sanctions and residency screens; a licence issued in Iran or a birthplace field reading Tehran can produce a refusal with no stated reason and no appeal.

aspect: SCENARIO - the car hire in Munich
description: Reza books a car for a client visit. At the desk his Iranian-issued licence and birthplace trigger a review. The agent is apologetic and says the system will not let her proceed. He takes three trains, arrives ninety minutes late, and explains the delay as traffic.
energy_note: Lying about small humiliations to stay professional.
